These studies will be compared with similar studies to be conducted as part of RISP.
Several of the biological-chemical proposals deal with the monitoring pesticides, chlorinated hydrocarbons, and other marine pollutants. Of particular significance is the proposed study of lead pollution in marine environments. Intensive studies have already been carried out concerning the Pleistocene marine geochemistry of lead. Lead is unique in that industrial and natural occurrences have different isotopic compositions making it possible to distinguish between these two kinds of lead in the marine environment. It seems unlikely that industrial lead pollution would be present in sufficient amounts to have significant effects in the water under the Ross Ice Shelf. The metabolism of the fish living in these waters is of special interest because such fish may permit us to determine what the natural distribution of lead among blood proteins should be.

These relationships may be used to establish reliable lead pollution indices in human blood.
Geological Investigations
Sediment cores will be obtained from the floor of the Ross Sea through the RISP hole. Gravity or piston-coring devices will be used to sample the uppermost strata, and a wire-line coring technique will be used for the deep core. There is a strong possibility that the sediments will contain a record which may also be recorded in the overlying ice. These superposed records may provide a system of internal checks on their interpretation.
